methods.title: Track contacts and review loop closure
methods.question: How should fixed lower contact of the retained east-idle be checked without treating the constant pivot [16,28] (and anchor [24,34]) as proof?

holds: applies_to includes idle loops; east-idle is a looping idle (loop=true).

Requirement 'named anchors, ground line and expected contact intervals' holds in adapted form: the brief names the lower contact edge, a constant pivot [16,28], anchor [24,34] and 'planted' for the whole loop (contact interval = entire 1600 ms loop). The ground line is the lowest opaque source row 27 (viewport row 33, directly above anchor y=34).
Procedure 'track contact-point coordinates independently from each frame's crop rectangle' is applicable and was applied: contact measured from pixels, not from rect/pivot metadata.

Check 'loop boundary obeys the same motion policy as internal transitions' is testable: east-4 and east-0 are byte-identical (71b35089...), so the 4->0 wrap has zero pixel change while internal transitions change only cyan pixels (0->1: 4 px, 1->2: 6 px, 2->3: 6 px, 3->4: 4 px, 4->0: 0 px).
unknown: Whether the pulse reads as convincing motion when watched continuously (R2); only stills and recorded tick transitions were reviewed in this trial.
unsuitable: Source 476-500 is about rig pivots/sockets for multi-part rigs (Unity pixel-unit pivots, socket JSON). The robot has no limbs or rig; only the general point 'pivots in logical pixel coordinates' transfers, and the consumer already does that. The socket contract does not transfer.

The method's proposed POC (three 16x16 frames with a foot anchor at (8,14) and a mutant at (9,14)) was not what executed; the executed receipt is shading-drift-mask, a mask-preservation fixture shared with the shading-drift method.
Foot/ground vocabulary: this robot has no feet or wheels; 'contact' is the body's lower edge.

methods.decision: Check fixed contact by measurement, not metadata: (1) decode each delivered frame and compare the full alpha mask to frame 0 (delivered: identical in all five frames, diff 0 px); (2) record the lowest opaque row and its column extent per frame (delivered: row 27, columns 11-20, width 10 in all five); (3) confirm the destination placement is unchanged (both retained captures record anchor [24,34] and pivot [16,28] for every sample, so a fixed source mask implies fixed destination contact at [8,6]+mask); (4) confirm the wrap transition 4->0 changes nothing. Constant pivots are a precondition only: the raw returned frames had the same constant pivot yet their masks differed from frame 0 by 27/63/12 px, the top opaque row moved 3->4->6 and frame 2's bottom row narrowed to columns 11-19, so equal pivots cannot prove planted contact.
methods.authority: Source suggestion (contact tracking independent of crop; D_t decomposition by silhouette/shade); explicit assignment (R3: lower contact planted without compensating pivot changes; constant pivot/anchor are CF-09 decisions, not universal rules); actual observations (mask and contact-row measurements above; capture anchor/pivot per sample); specialist construction (choice of 'lowest opaque row + column extent + whole-mask equality' as the contact metric).

proof.limits: Receipt text: 'Proves mask preservation in this idle fixture, not a convincing breathing action or general world-space foot planting.' It ran against pixl/poc.py fixtures, not this robot; it does not establish CF-09 contact, motion quality or acceptance. The method's proposed timeline-fixture POC is not evidenced by this receipt.

methods.next_action: Keep the delivered frames and placement unchanged. For any future revision of east-1..3, rerun the mask/contact-row measurement against the unchanged anchor/pivot and view the sequence in the destination; a continuous-playback human review of R2/R3 remains the open acceptance step.

methods.title: Author duration and event semantics per frame
methods.question: Should the provider preview's uniform 100 ms per frame (total 500 ms) replace the authored durations [800,120,160,120,400] (total 1600 ms) on a cold import?

holds: applies_to includes sprite animation and idle loops.
Requirement 'ordered frame IDs, positive durations and loop or one-shot policy' holds: east-0..east-4, durations all positive, loop=true in src/animation.ts.
Procedure 'store durations explicitly rather than assuming uniform FPS' holds: durations are per-frame fields in the authored clip.

Procedure 'define half-open time intervals' holds in the actual adapter: frameAt uses `at < duration_ms`, giving [0,800)->0, [800,920)->1, [920,1080)->2, [1080,1200)->3, [1200,1600)->4 and wrap at 1600 via modulo.

Check 'playback reaches the expected frame at boundary times' was evaluated against the adapter logic (table in import_decision) and is consistent with the retained browser captures: observed transitions at ~800/816.7, 933.3, 1083.3, 1200/1216.6 and 1616.6 ms, i.e. within one ~16.7 ms animation-frame tick after each authored boundary, with 2 wraps, 10 transitions and 0 skips at both 1x and 3x in both captures.

Pitfall 'unspecified preview FPS must not overwrite authored durations' is the directly relevant guidance: the uniform [100 x5] comes from the workbench inspect text for image 01e5a451-2b3b-4249-b710-348c267a0ec9, not from the owner or the adapter.
unknown: Whether the PixelLab durations field is a default preview rate or user-settable metadata for that image; no provider connection in this session, so it was not re-queried.
Perceived calmness of the 400 ms pulse window under continuous viewing (R2) is not established by boundary arithmetic.
unsuitable: Procedure 'name anticipation, action, impact and settle events': the consumer has no event channel; naming is optional documentation here, not a requirement.
Source example cadence (80/50/33/100/33/50/120 ms) and the example JSON duration_ms 120 'settle' are illustrations of unequal cadence; their numbers do not transfer.
Source 948-960 is a CSS box-shadow demo keyframe (pulse 1.2s steps(1) infinite with blur(1.4px) and translate(-2px,2px) at 50%); its period and effects do not transfer.

methods.decision: Retain the authored sequence [800,120,160,120,400] ms (1600 ms loop) and reject replacing it with uniform 5x100 ms. Under the actual frameAt adapter the two timelines select different frames at 10 of the 11 sampled times (all except t=0); the uniform timeline would compress the 400 ms pulse window (frames 1-3) into 300 ms repeated every 500 ms with a 100 ms rest, contradicting the brief's 'long resting pose and brief display pulse ... occasional idle signal'. The retained captures already evidence recorded playback under the authored durations; no capture evidences the uniform timeline.
methods.authority: Explicit assignment (CF-09: durations, pivot, anchor are this assignment's decisions; R2 requires playback under the declared unequal durations; R5 declared timing); source suggestion (explicit durations, half-open intervals, preview FPS must not overwrite authored durations); actual observations (provider inspect text, adapter code, scratch evaluation, capture tick transitions); specialist construction (treating <=16.7 ms RAF latency after each boundary as consistent with authored timing).

proof.limits: Receipt text: 'Tests looping frame selection with half-open intervals, not audiovisual synchronization or action-event dispatch.' It exercised the fixture implementation in pixl/poc.py with durations 80/40/120, not this consumer's frameAt. The method's proposed second acceptance ('impact event at 120 fires once per loop crossing') is not covered by the executed receipt. The consumer adapter was evaluated separately by the scratch re-implementation and by the retained browser captures.

methods.next_action: Do not change src/animation.ts. If any importer reads provider frame metadata, treat its durations as preview information and map onto the authored durations; if a different engine is targeted, produce that engine's own boundary observation.
